rules.plain: Only VA-accredited agents and attorneys may receive fees for representation on a VA claim.
rules.trigger: fee_requested == true AND NOT (verification.status IN ['verified_by_number','exact_name_state'] AND verification.kind IN ['attorney','claims_agent'])

rules.plain: Recognized Veterans Service Organizations and their accredited representatives are not permitted to receive fees.
rules.trigger: fee_requested == true AND (verification.kind == 'vso_rep' OR claims_to_be_vso == true)

rules.plain: Agents and attorneys may charge only for representation provided after VA has issued notice of an initial decision on the claim. Help filing a first claim cannot be charged for.
Fees above 33 1/3 percent of past-due benefits are presumed unreasonable.
Fees up to 20 percent of past-due benefits are presumed reasonable. Fees between 20 and 33 1/3 percent are not presumed either way; ask why.

The regulation's reasonableness presumptions are measured against past-due benefits. A fee based on future monthly payments (for example 'five times your monthly increase') falls outside them; ask the representative to explain it in a written agreement.
Fees may be fixed, hourly, a percentage, or a mix, but every fee agreement must be in writing, signed by both sides, include the VA file number and fee terms, and be filed with VA within 30 days.

rules.cite: VA guidance on protecting VA.gov sign-in (to confirm and link on Day 2)
rules.plain: Never share your VA.gov, ID.me or Login.gov username, password or codes with a helper.

free_help.plain: Accredited VSO representatives help with VA claims for free.
